name: Urgent Eye
description: A 15-episode series on the ocular emergencies that walk into optometry practice — from the red eye and sudden vision loss to chemical burns and open globes.

episodes.title: Red Eye Triage: The Three Questions That Separate Emergency from Routine
episodes.description: The pain, vision, and photophobia triage questions, the slit lamp findings that demand same-day referral, and the empiric treatment errors to avoid.

episodes.title: Sudden Painless Vision Loss: CRAO, CRVO, and the Time-Critical Workup
episodes.description: The sudden painless loss differential, the immediate fundus exam, and the stroke risk and carotid workup urgency.

episodes.title: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma: The Foggy, Painful, Mid-Dilated Pupil
episodes.description: The acute ACG presentation, the immediate IOP-lowering protocol (acetazolamide, pilocarpine, hyperosmotic), and the laser iridotomy timing.

episodes.title: Contact Lens Keratitis: The Ulcer Depth, Culture, and the Antibiotic Protocol
episodes.description: The ulcer assessment (size, depth, location), the culture indications, and the fortified antibiotic vs fluoroquinolone monotherapy decision.

episodes.title: Chemical Burns: The 15-Minute Irrigation and the Limbal Stem Cell Assessment
episodes.description: The immediate copious irrigation, the pH check and recheck, the Roper-Hall and Dua classification, and the stem cell damage prognostication.

episodes.title: Traumatic Iritis: The Ciliary Flush, Cells, and Flare and the Steroid Decision
episodes.description: The ciliary flush and photophobia presentation, the slit lamp cell and flare grading, and the cycloplegia and topical steroid protocol.

episodes.title: Hyphema: The Layered Blood, the Sickling Test, and the Bed Rest Debate
episodes.description: The hyphema grading, the sickle cell screening, the rebleed risk, and the activity restriction and IOP control and surgical evacuation threshold.

episodes.title: Orbital Cellulitis vs Preseptal: The CT Scan and the IV Antibiotic Decision
episodes.description: The clinical signs of orbital cellulitis (proptosis, restricted motility, RAPD), the CT indication, and the urgent ENT or ophthalmology referral.

episodes.title: Retinal Detachment: The Flashes, Floaters, Curtain, and the Same-Day Referral
episodes.description: The rhegmatogenous RD symptoms, the peripheral exam for the break, the macula-on vs macula-off urgency, and the immediate surgical referral.

episodes.title: Giant Cell Arteritis: The Jaw Claudication, the ESR/CRP, and the IV Steroids
episodes.description: The age-60+ headache and vision loss, the immediate ESR and CRP, the high-dose IV steroid before biopsy, and the bilateral blindness risk.

episodes.title: Endophthalmitis: The Post-Cataract, Post-Injection, and Post-Trauma Causes
episodes.description: The postoperative endophthalmitis window, the hypopyon and pain presentation, the vitreous tap and inject protocol, and the visual prognosis.

episodes.title: Open Globe Injury: The Peaking Pupil, the CT for IOFB, and the Surgical Shield
episodes.description: The open globe signs (peaked pupil, shallow AC, hyphema), the no-pressure-shield protection, the CT for foreign body, and the urgent surgery.

episodes.title: Traumatic Optic Neuropathy: The Fracture, the Steroid Controversy, and the Prognosis
episodes.description: The traumatic vision loss with a normal fundus, the CT for canal fracture, the high-dose steroid debate (CRASH trial), and the prognosis.

episodes.title: Eyelid Lacerations: The Canalicular Involvement and the Repair Timing
episodes.description: The eyelid laceration assessment (canalicular, orbital fat, levator), the tetanus status, and the repair timing and the referral.

episodes.title: When to Send to the Emergency Department: The Optometrist's Triage Map
episodes.description: A summary triage map of the eye emergencies that demand ED vs urgent ophthalmology vs next-day referral, and the documentation for the handoff.
